definitions.explanation: A formal way to say 'this year.' Used in official documents, business correspondence, speeches, and formal greetings.

examples.japanese: {本年|ほんねん}もよろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。
examples.english: I look forward to your continued support this year.

examples.japanese: {本年度|ほんねんど}の{予算|よさん}が{承認|しょうにん}された。
examples.english: This fiscal year's budget was approved.

examples.japanese: {本年|ほんねん}は{創業|そうぎょう}50{周年|しゅうねん}を{迎|むか}える{記念|きねん}すべき{年|とし}でございます。
examples.english: This year is a memorable year as we celebrate our 50th anniversary.

notes:
A formal equivalent of {今年|ことし} (this year). Used exclusively in formal writing and speech, such as business letters, official reports, New Year's greetings, and public announcements.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {本年|ほんねん}もよろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします: standard New Year greeting in business
- {本年度|ほんねんど}: this fiscal/academic year
- {本年中|ほんねんちゅう}: during this year
- {本年|ほんねん}は: as for this year (opening phrase in speeches)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {今年|ことし}: this year — the standard, everyday word; used in all registers
- {昨年|さくねん}: last year — the formal equivalent of {去年|きょねん}
- {来年|らいねん}: next year — used in both formal and casual registers

REGISTER:
Highly formal. Using {本年|ほんねん} in casual conversation would sound stiff and unnatural. In everyday speech, always use {今年|ことし} instead.
